nodes.speaker: Councillor Hargrove
nodes.text: I don't receive visitors without an appointment. Who let you in here?

nodes.speaker: Edmund
nodes.text: My name is Edmund Hale. My wife is dead. She was investigating your Whitmore Street properties.

nodes.speaker: Councillor Hargrove
nodes.text: I'm very sorry for your loss. But I have nothing to do with whatever your wife involved herself in.

choices.text: I have a witness. A resident of number twelve, Whitmore Street. She'll testify about the roof collapse.
I work at the Chronicle. I can make your name very prominent in tomorrow's edition.
[Grab him by the collar.] A child died in your building. You paid the family to disappear. Tell me what you did.

nodes.speaker: Councillor Hargrove
nodes.text: Be very careful, Mr Hale. You are making accusations about a city councillor based on the word of a slum-dweller.

nodes.speaker: Councillor Hargrove
nodes.text: The Chronicle runs on my advertising budget. You go ahead and test that relationship.
Edmund is removed from the estate by force.
nodes.journal_entry: They threw me out. But Hargrove was frightened — genuinely frightened. He knows something.

nodes.speaker: Councillor Hargrove
nodes.text: Your wife wrote to the Chronicle. I know that. Mr Crane assured me that letter would go no further. I suggest you speak to him.
nodes.journal_entry: Hargrove knows about Clara's letter. He said Arthur Crane assured him it would go no further. Arthur. Why did Arthur tell him that?
